facts.title: What did Chandrayaan-3 achieve on 23 August 2023?
facts.copy: It successfully soft-landed on the Moon.
facts.verifiedExcerpt: August 23, 2023 — Chandrayaan-3 has successfully soft-landed on the moon.

facts.title: What was Aryabhata in India’s space history?
facts.copy: Aryabhata was India’s first satellite; it was designed and fabricated in India and launched on 19 April 1975.
facts.verifiedExcerpt: The Aryabhata spacecraft, named after the famous Indian astronomer, was India's first satellite; it was completely designed and fabricated in India and launched by a Soviet Kosmos-3M rocket from Kapustin Yar on April 19, 1975.

facts.title: What first-attempt milestone did India’s Mars Orbiter Mission achieve?
facts.copy: It entered Martian orbit on 24 September 2014 on its first attempt.
facts.verifiedExcerpt: Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM), the truly maiden interplanetary mission of ISRO, launched on November 5, 2013 successfully got inserted into Martian orbit on September 24, 2014 in its first attempt.

facts.title: What happens to some light in the Raman effect?
facts.copy: A small portion of scattered light has wavelengths different from those of the original light.
facts.sourceTitle: Sir Venkata Raman — Nobel Prize Facts
facts.verifiedExcerpt: In 1928 Venkata Raman discovered that a small portion of the scattered light acquires other wavelengths than that of the original light.

facts.title: What distinction did C-DAC’s PARAM 8000 hold?
facts.copy: It was India’s first giga-scale supercomputer.
facts.verifiedExcerpt: PARAM 8000, India's 1st Giga-scale supercomputer in 1990

facts.title: What was Apsara, and when did it become operational?
facts.copy: Apsara was Asia’s first research reactor and became operational at Trombay in August 1956.
facts.sourceTitle: Apsara research reactor — Press Information Bureau
facts.verifiedExcerpt: “Apsara”, the first research reactor in Asia became operational in Trombay campus of Bhabha Atomic Research Centre in August 1956.

facts.title: When did the Dandi March begin from Satyagraha Ashram?
facts.copy: It began on 12 March 1930.
facts.verifiedExcerpt: 12 March | 1930 | Dandi March commences from Satyagraha Ashram.

facts.title: On what date was the Quit India resolution adopted?
facts.copy: It was adopted on 8 August 1942; Gandhi gave the call “Do or Die.”
facts.verifiedExcerpt: 8 August | 1942 | 'Quit India' resolution adopted; gave the call 'Do or Die'.

facts.title: Where and when was the Indian National Congress’s first session held, and who presided?
facts.copy: It was held in Bombay from 28–30 December 1885, with Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee as president.
facts.verifiedExcerpt: 1st Session | Bombay | Dec. 28-30, 1885 | Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee

facts.title: Where did India’s first passenger train run, and on what date?
facts.copy: It ran from Bori Bunder in Mumbai to Thane on 16 April 1853.
facts.verifiedExcerpt: The first passenger train in India ran from Bori Bunder, Mumbai, to Thane on 16 April 1853.

facts.title: What happened to the Asokan stupa at Sanchi during Sunga times?
facts.copy: It was enlarged, faced with stone, and decorated with balustrades, staircases and a harmika at the top.
facts.sourceTitle: Buddhist Monuments at Sanchi — Archaeological Survey of India
facts.verifiedExcerpt: During Sunga times, several edifices were raised at Sanchi and its surrounding hills. The Asokan stupa was enlarged and faced with stones and decorated with balustrades, staircases and a harmika on the top.

facts.title: Who became India’s first prime minister on 15 August 1947?
facts.copy: Jawaharlal Nehru became the first Prime Minister of free India on 15 August 1947.
facts.sourceTitle: India’s First Prime Minister — Nehru Portal
facts.verifiedExcerpt: Became the first Prime Minister of free India ... 15, August 1947

facts.title: Which meridian is used to calculate Indian Standard Time?
facts.copy: Indian Standard Time is calculated from the 82°30′E meridian passing through Mirzapur.
facts.verifiedExcerpt: The Indian Standard Time is calculated from 82°30’E meridian passing through Mirzapur.

facts.title: How many global biodiversity hotspots does India contain parts of?
facts.copy: India contains parts of four global biodiversity hotspots.
facts.sourceTitle: India’s Fourth National Report to the Convention on Biological Diversity
facts.verifiedExcerpt: India has four global biodiversity hot spots (Eastern Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, and Sundaland).

facts.title: Where is Barren Island, and what is it known for?
facts.copy: Barren Island is in the East Andaman Sea and is the only active volcano in South Asia.
facts.sourceTitle: Textures in Pyroclastic Rocks — Geological Survey of India
facts.verifiedExcerpt: Barren Island in the east Andaman Sea ... is the only active volcano in south Asia.

facts.title: Which rivers form the delta where the Sundarbans mangrove forest lies?
facts.copy: The Sundarbans lies on the Ganges–Brahmaputra–Meghna delta on the Bay of Bengal.
facts.sourceTitle: The Sundarbans — UNESCO World Heritage Centre
facts.verifiedExcerpt: The Sundarbans mangrove forest ... lies on the delta of the Ganges, Brahmaputra and Meghna rivers on the Bay of Bengal.

facts.title: Which mountain chain is older than the Himalaya and influences India’s monsoon?
facts.copy: The Western Ghats are older than the Himalaya, and their high montane forests influence Indian monsoon weather patterns.
facts.sourceTitle: Western Ghats — UNESCO World Heritage Centre
facts.verifiedExcerpt: Older than the Himalaya mountains, the mountain chain of the Western Ghats ... The site’s high montane forest ecosystems influence the Indian monsoon weather pattern.

facts.title: In which river-valley floodplain is Kaziranga National Park located?
facts.copy: Kaziranga National Park is in Assam, in the Brahmaputra Valley floodplain.
facts.sourceTitle: Kaziranga National Park — UNESCO World Heritage Centre
facts.verifiedExcerpt: located in the State of Assam it is the single largest undisturbed and representative area in the Brahmaputra Valley floodplain.

facts.title: Which constitutional article abolishes untouchability?
facts.copy: Article 17 abolishes untouchability, forbids its practice in any form, and makes enforcement of any disability arising from it an offence punishable by law.
facts.verifiedExcerpt: “Untouchability” is abolished and its practice in any form is forbidden. The enforcement of any disability arising out of “Untouchability” shall be an offence punishable in accordance with law.

facts.title: What education does Article 21A require the State to provide?
facts.copy: The State must provide free and compulsory education to children aged six to fourteen, as determined by law.
facts.verifiedExcerpt: The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years in such manner as the State may, by law, determine.

facts.title: Are the Directive Principles of State Policy enforceable in court?
facts.copy: No. Article 37 says they are not enforceable by any court, but are fundamental to governance and the State must apply them when making laws.
facts.verifiedExcerpt: The provisions contained in this Part shall not be enforceable by any court, but the principles therein laid down are nevertheless fundamental in the governance of the country and it shall be the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.

facts.title: What cultural duty does Article 51A place on every citizen?
facts.copy: Every citizen has a fundamental duty to value and preserve the rich heritage of India’s composite culture.
facts.verifiedExcerpt: (f) to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture;

facts.title: What principle governs elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies under Article 326?
facts.copy: The Constitution provides that elections to the House of the People (Lok Sabha) and State Legislative Assemblies are based on adult suffrage.
facts.verifiedExcerpt: 326. Elections to the House of the People and to the Legislative Assemblies of States to be on the basis of adult suffrage.

facts.title: Which language and script does Article 343 designate for the Union?
facts.copy: Article 343 names Hindi in Devanagari script as the official language of the Union; this does not say that Hindi is India’s national language.
facts.sourceTitle: Constitutional Provisions — Department of Official Language
facts.verifiedExcerpt: Article 343. Official language of the Union- The official language of the Union shall be Hindi in Devnagari script.

facts.title: What is the International Court of Justice’s role within the United Nations?
facts.copy: It is the United Nations’ principal judicial organ.
facts.sourceTitle: The Court — International Court of Justice
facts.verifiedExcerpt: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations (UN).

facts.title: On what date did the World Health Organization’s Constitution come into force?
facts.copy: 7 April 1948, a date now observed each year as World Health Day.
facts.verifiedExcerpt: WHO’s Constitution came into force on 7 April 1948 – a date we now celebrate every year as World Health Day.

facts.title: In what year was UNICEF established?
facts.copy: UNICEF was established in 1946, after the Second World War.
facts.verifiedExcerpt: The United Nations International Children’s Emergency Fund (UNICEF) was established in 1946, in the aftermath of World War II.

facts.title: In what year was the International Labour Organization created?
facts.copy: The ILO was created in 1919 as part of the Treaty of Versailles.
facts.verifiedExcerpt: The ILO was created in 1919, as part of the Treaty of Versailles that ended World War I

facts.title: When and where was the Food and Agriculture Organization created?
facts.copy: FAO was created on 16 October 1945 in Quebec, Canada.
facts.verifiedExcerpt: On 16 October 1945, 42 countries acted in Quebec, Canada, to create FAO — the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations.

facts.title: When and where was UNESCO’s Constitution adopted?
facts.copy: It was adopted in London on 16 November 1945.
facts.verifiedExcerpt: Adopted in London on 16 November 1945

facts.title: Which Indian state is associated with Sattriya traditions?
facts.copy: Assam.
facts.verifiedExcerpt: National Projects of Support to Kuttiyattam - the age-old Sanskrit theatre of Kerala - Chhau dances of eastern India and Sattriya traditions of Assam have been launched subsequently.

facts.title: What are Ajanta’s paintings and sculptures known for?
facts.copy: They are masterpieces of Buddhist religious art.
facts.sourceTitle: Ajanta Caves — UNESCO World Heritage Centre
facts.verifiedExcerpt: The paintings and sculptures of Ajanta, considered masterpieces of Buddhist religious art, have had a considerable artistic influence.

facts.title: How many Olympic gold medals has India’s men’s hockey team won?
facts.copy: Eight, including six consecutive golds from 1928 to 1956.
facts.sourceTitle: Indian hockey men at the Olympics — Olympics.com
facts.verifiedExcerpt: The Indian men’s hockey team has won eight Olympic gold medals in all, six of them in a row (from 1928-1956) and added two more at Tokyo 1964 and Moscow 1980.

facts.title: When were India’s GST laws implemented?
facts.copy: On 1 July 2017.
facts.verifiedExcerpt: On July 1, 2017, GST laws were implemented, replacing a complex web of Central and State taxes.

facts.title: In what year was the BSE founded?
facts.copy: 1875; BSE describes itself as Asia’s oldest exchange.
facts.verifiedExcerpt: Founded in 1875, BSE is Asia’s oldest exchange.

facts.title: Which institution has the sole right to issue banknotes in India?
facts.copy: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
facts.verifiedExcerpt: In terms of Section 22 of the Act, Reserve Bank has the sole right to issue banknotes in India.
